     2	
     3	**Team:** 075
     4	**Platform:** OpenEgiz v1.0.4
     5	**Repository:** https://github.com/openegiz-contest/team-075
     6	
     7	## Project Overview
     8	
     9	EcoMine is an environmental monitoring and digital twin prototype for mining operations.
    10	
    11	The system simulates mining truck telemetry, processes environmental measurements, stores time-series data, updates a digital twin, and visualizes operational indicators through Grafana.
    12	
    13	The main goal is to demonstrate how mining enterprises can monitor environmental performance and identify potentially high-emission operating conditions.
    14	
    15	## Mine Model and Digital Twin
    16	
    17	The prototype represents a simulated open-pit mining haulage operation with four trucks.
    18	
    19	Each truck generates telemetry containing:
    20	- Truck identifier and type
    21	- Ore transported, in tonnes
    22	- Energy consumption equivalent, in kWh
    23	- Water consumption, in cubic metres
    24	- CO2 emissions, in kilograms
    25	- Timestamp
    26	
    27	The Eclipse Ditto digital twin is represented by the Thing ID:
    28	
    29	`ecomine:smart-mine`
    30	
    31	The twin is updated through the Ditto HTTP API.
    32	
    33	Implementation:
    34	- `examples/ecomine/mqtt_simulator.py`
    35	- `examples/ecomine/ditto_bridge.py`
    36	
    37	## Architecture
    38	
    39	Data flow:
    40	
    41	Mining Truck Simulator
    42	→ MQTT / Mosquitto
    43	→ InfluxDB Writers
    44	→ InfluxDB
    45	→ Grafana Dashboard and Risk Alert
    46	
    47	In parallel:
    48	
    49	MQTT / Mosquitto
    50	→ Ditto Bridge
    51	→ Eclipse Ditto Digital Twin
    52	
    53	Technologies:
    54	- Python
    55	- Docker Compose
    56	- MQTT / Eclipse Mosquitto
    57	- InfluxDB
    58	- Eclipse Ditto
    59	- Grafana
    60	
    61	## Modules and What-if Scenarios
    62	
    63	| Module or What-if Scenario | What it does | How to see it on the Stand | How to undo it (scenarios) |
    64	|---|---|---|---|
    65	| Truck Telemetry Simulation | Generates synthetic telemetry for four mining trucks | MQTT telemetry and Grafana | Stop the simulator container |
    66	| Environmental Monitoring | Records CO2, water, energy and ore measurements | Grafana dashboard | Not applicable |
    67	| Environmental Risk Analysis | Classifies simulated CO2 measurements as NORMAL, WARNING or CRITICAL | Environmental Risk panel and service logs | Not applicable |
    68	| Digital Twin Synchronization | Updates the EcoMine Thing in Eclipse Ditto | Ditto HTTP API | Not applicable |
    69	| Critical Risk Alert | Detects critical risk values using a Grafana alert rule | Grafana Alerting | Not applicable |
    70	
    71	No interactive what-if scenario has been verified. The current prototype demonstrates continuous telemetry processing and risk monitoring.
    72	
    73	## What Works and What Does Not
    74	
    75	Verified locally:
    76	- Four EcoMine Docker services start successfully.
    77	- MQTT telemetry is generated.
    78	- InfluxDB accepts telemetry and risk measurements (HTTP 204).
    79	- Eclipse Ditto accepts digital twin updates (HTTP 204).
    80	- Five Grafana panels display environmental and operational measurements.
    81	- A Grafana critical-risk alert has been observed in FIRING state.
    82	
    83	Not yet verified:
    84	- Fresh installation on a separate computer.
    85	- Automatic provisioning of the Grafana dashboard and alert on a clean deployment.
    86	- Interactive operational what-if scenarios.
    87	
    88	## Data and Assumptions
    89	
    90	All mining telemetry is synthetic.
    91	
    92	The prototype does not use confidential enterprise data or personal data.
    93	
    94	The risk classification is a demonstration rule based on CO2 mass per simulated telemetry record:
    95	
    96	- NORMAL: CO2 below 150 kg
    97	- WARNING: CO2 from 150 kg to below 200 kg
    98	- CRITICAL: CO2 of 200 kg or above
    99	
   100	These thresholds are prototype assumptions, not regulatory or industrial safety limits.
   101	
   102	The data is intended for software demonstration and does not represent validated measurements from a real mine.
   103	
   104	## Mine Visualization
   105	
   106	Grafana dashboard:
   107	
   108	`http://localhost:3000`
   109	
   110	The dashboard includes:
   111	1. CO2 Emissions
   112	2. Water Consumption
   113	3. Energy Consumption
   114	4. Ore Transportation
   115	5. Environmental Risk
   116	
   117	The Grafana alerting interface displays the critical environmental risk alert.
   118	
   119	These are local development addresses. External Stand URLs have not yet been verified.
   120	
   121	## Limitations
   122	
   123	- The system currently uses simulated truck data.
   124	- No physical mining equipment is connected.
   125	- Risk thresholds are illustrative.
   126	- The digital twin represents aggregated mining telemetry rather than a fully modeled industrial mine.
   127	- Dashboard and alert provisioning require further automation.
   128	- No interactive what-if scenario is currently implemented.
   129	
   130	## Presentation
   131	
   132	`presentation.pdf` will be added to the repository root.
   133

    42

    44	
    45	`deploy/compose/ecomine.yml`
    46	
    47	A valid InfluxDB token must be provided through the
    48	`ECOMINE_INFLUX_TOKEN` environment variable.
    49	
    50	Run from the repository root:
    51	
    52	`docker compose --env-file deploy/compose/.env -f deploy/compose/docker-compose.yml -f deploy/compose/ecomine.yml up -d --build`
    53	
    54	## Local Interfaces
    55	
    56	- Grafana: http://localhost:3000
    57	- InfluxDB: http://localhost:8086
    58	- Eclipse Ditto API: http://localhost:8080
    59	
    60	## Current Limitations
    61	
    62	- All mining telemetry is synthetic.
    63	- Risk thresholds are illustrative.
    64	- Grafana dashboard and alert provisioning are not yet automated.
    65	- Fresh installation on another computer has not been verified.
    66	
    67	For submission details, see `SUBMISSION.md`.
    68	
    69	---
    70	
    71	## Original OpenEgiz Documentation
    72	
    73	# <Team name>: a digital mine on OpenEgiz
    74	
    75	> Team Repository of the contest “Digital Mine on OpenEgiz”. **Replace the contents of this file with the instructions for your Submission.** The AI Jury runs the Submission strictly by these instructions, from scratch, in the Judge Environment. Accepted languages: English, Kazakh, Russian.

What AI agents build from this Template without a Concept is the Default Solution, published on the [contest site](https://openegiz-contest.github.io/) as the low bar: a Submission that does not go beyond it gets low levels in the Rubric. AI agents read [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md).
    78	
    79	## Running
    80	
    81	Requirements (Docker, `make`, Windows/WSL2 setup) are in [OPENEGIZ.md](OPENEGIZ.md) / [OPENEGIZ.ru.md](OPENEGIZ.ru.md).
    82	
    83	```bash
    84	sudo apt install -y make   # if make is missing (clean Ubuntu)
    85	make up            # the OpenEgiz platform
    86	make example-mine  # the Example Mine: twins, simulator, dashboard
    87	```
    88	
    89	Replace these commands with the commands of your Submission. The Submission must start by following these instructions without manual intervention (Rules, clause 6.4); downloading datasets and models and building are also listed here.
    90	
    91	## What to open
    92	
    93	- Grafana: the address and login are printed by `make up`.
    94	- <where to see the mine visualization, which dashboards>
    95

    97
